B. Is this measure already running in West Uusimaa wellbeing services county (or in the HUS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure reduce deaths among the people it reaches, and by how much?
Measure: Smoking cessation started at the first specialist visit. Every current smoker with suspected lung cancer gets cessation medication and counselling at the first visit, as part of preparing for curative treatment.
supported_en: Patients with early-stage lung cancer who quit after diagnosis had 33% lower all-cause mortality (HR 0.67), according to an observational study in Annals of Internal Medicine (2021).
not_supported_en: The study does not show how many smokers offered medication and counselling at the first visit actually quit, so the effect on everyone reached is smaller than 0.67.
summary_en: B: I found no public sign that this is already running. HUS's lung cancer pathway page says patients see a nurse for guidance at the first visit and that quitting completely is key to prognosis. LUVN's site lists the free online self-help programmes on Terveyskylä, run by HUS, which need no referral; neither page describes medication and counselling for every smoker at the first visit. A: An observational study from Moscow (Annals of Internal Medicine 2021, 517 patients with early-stage lung cancer) found an all-cause mortality HR of 0.67 (95% CI 0.53–0.85) for those who quit after diagnosis; that applies to people who quit, not to everyone the programme reaches.
unanswered_en: I found no page from HUS or LUVN about a routine cessation service with medication for patients with suspected lung cancer, such as a dedicated cessation nurse at the lung clinic.
